reader.requirement: At 1985 a PERFORM's procedure-name-1 and procedure-name-2 must name only paragraphs or sections of its own program (a reference into a containing, contained, sibling or separately compiled program is refused), and another program's statements run within a PERFORM range only through CALL and EXIT PROGRAM.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.Cite: the message quotes §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR13 at 85, §2023:14.9.28.3 SR12/SR13 later; the resolution is one code

reader.edition-search: the procedure table is built per bound unit (ProcedureTableBuilder), so another program's paragraphs are never candidates at any edition; grep DialectLevel|CobolVersion in ControlFlowBinder.cs and ProcedureTableBuilder.cs found only the citation choice
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover an unknown procedure-name and GO TO DEPENDING; not exercised are PERFORM into a contained, containing, sibling or separately compiled program, a same-named paragraph in another program, and a range that reaches another program through CALL

reader.notes: Procedure-name resolution consults only the current unit's procedure table, so every cross-program reference is refused with COBOL1639 quoting GR13, and a same-named paragraph resolves to the program's own; the CALL/EXIT PROGRAM path runs the other program's statements and returns into the range.

refuter.evidence: At --std 85: a contained program's 'PERFORM P1 OF S1', where S1 is a section of the containing program and the contained program has its own P1 in another section, is refused (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/g13_qual.cob: COBOL1639 'PERFORM P1 OF S1 names no procedure ... §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.6'), so a qualifier cannot reach into another program; a contained program's PERFORM of the containing program's USE GLOBAL declarative section is refused (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/g13_decl.cob: COBOL1639 PERFORM 'DGF'). The run-time half: a contained program's PERFORM K1 THRU K2 whose range does a failing OPEN on the container's GLOBAL file runs the container's USE GLOBAL declarative and then returns into the range (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/g13_declrun.cob, runs/g13_declrun-001: K1 / DECL FS=35 / K2 / K DONE / BACK). That declarative is another program's statement obeyed within the range without CALL, but it is selected by the USE precedence rule §1985:X.5.5.4 GR1b (cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.5.5.4 GR1b ... the text is in GR1b'), the more specific rule, and reached by the implicit declarative transfer of §1985:IV.4.4.2, not by the PERFORM; read that way it is no breach of GR13. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR13', 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.6'.
